profiles.meeting_scenario: Feature-Factory is being piloted inside a SaaS company's Atlas billing platform to automate integration of a backlog request called "invoice reminder rules" using WatsonX.ai. In this planning meeting, the participants need to decide what the first pilot will cover, what inputs will be fed into the automation pipeline, how validation will happen, who owns each preparation task, and what must be ready by Friday for leadership visibility. The agenda is to confirm pilot scope, identify the documentation and repositories the system will parse, assign setup and coordination work, and agree on the timeline for a Friday checkpoint. The expected outcome is a shared-seeming plan for the pilot implementation, responsibilities, and end-of-week deliverable.

members.name: Sara Kim
members.role: Staff Software Engineer, Integration Platform Lead
members.expertise: Developer tooling, CI/CD pipelines, monorepo dependency analysis, backend service integration
members.background: Sara has spent five years building internal platform automation for the company's Java and Node services, including code generation templates and merge-gating workflows for backend teams.
members.private_state: She wants the Feature-Factory pilot to succeed without disrupting release operations, so she is quietly steering it toward a narrow, backend-heavy implementation that can fit into existing platform support capacity this sprint.
hidden_assumptions: A pilot proves Feature-Factory if it can generate mergeable backend pull requests that pass CI and dependency checks, even if no user-facing surface is included yet.
When a feature request is named in planning, the relevant scope is the engineering slice already broken down for implementation rather than the full business-facing request title.

Current architecture documentation means in-repository ADRs, OpenAPI specs, and code-level configuration that the parser can consume directly; external diagrams are reference material, not source of truth.
A Friday delivery in sprint planning means end of day Pacific with artifacts ready for engineers to review, not necessarily ready for an executive audience earlier that day.
Staging refers to the shared engineering staging cluster with synthetic data and default feature-flag settings.

members.name: Daniel Ortiz
members.expertise: AI pilot rollout, cross-functional planning, stakeholder demos, enterprise software adoption
members.background: Daniel previously worked as a solutions architect for internal AI programs and now runs pilot planning for generative tooling initiatives across product and engineering teams.
members.private_state: He needs a visible, credible win for the steering committee, so he is implicitly aiming for a pilot that looks like a full customer-facing feature integration with demo-ready evidence rather than just an engineering handoff.
hidden_assumptions: A pilot only counts as a convincing feature integration if it reproduces the end-user or operator-visible part of the request, not just hidden service changes.
A named feature request refers to the original customer or operations outcome, including any configuration screens needed to use it.
Current architecture documentation includes the latest Confluence pages, Miro system maps, and domain-owner updates, even if those details have not yet been mirrored into the code repositories.
A Friday commitment means materials are ready before the 10:00 UTC governance review where pilots are shown to leadership.
Staging means the UAT environment with a realistic tenant configuration, audit logging enabled, and near-production workflows.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the "invoice reminder rules" feature
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to pilot the "invoice reminder rules" integration.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the pilot covers backend work in the billing-service and related API/schema updates needed to support reminder-rule logic, but not the admin configuration screen.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the pilot covers the full operations-facing capability, including the admin UI/settings flow needed for customer operations to configure reminder rules.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The feature name naturally compresses the business request and the engineering subtask into the same phrase, so both hear familiar wording and do not feel a need to restate boundaries that seem already implied.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the pilot should be "integration-ready by Friday."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means generated pull requests are opened, CI is green, and the work is ready for normal engineering review by Friday end of day Pacific.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means there is a staging-deployed walkthrough package with screenshots, audit notes, and a coherent story ready before the Friday 10:00 UTC steering review.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In planning meetings, "ready" is a common handoff word whose precise bar depends on role, and each participant assumes the other's bar matches their own because the timeline sounds routine and achievable.

misalignment_points.topic: Which documents are the "current architecture docs"
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to feed Feature-Factory the current architecture documentation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes this means the repo-local ADRs, OpenAPI definitions, and service config files that the parser already ingests automatically.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes this includes the recent Confluence replatforming notes and Miro diagrams from the billing domain team that describe service boundaries and workflow updates.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both know that architecture docs exist and both know the system consumes documentation, so they skip enumerating the corpus and assume "current" is an obvious shared set.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the pilot will be validated in staging.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the shared engineering staging cluster used for smoke tests with synthetic billing data and default flags.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the FinOps UAT tenant, which his group informally also calls staging because it is the pre-demo environment used for leadership reviews.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both environments are casually labeled "staging" across teams, and because validation is being discussed at a high level rather than as an environment-request task, neither notices they are picturing different targets.
